correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the two constructible kernel families over C, not a decomposition of the boundary. On a conic in a plane missing p the three entries of O(-4) -> O(-2)^3 are a basis of binary quadrics. By Serre duality the induced H^1 map is an isomorphism, so the rank-two cokernel has degree -2 and no sections and splits as O(-1)^2 on P^1. Its nonzero maps to the degree -1 target are onto and are parametrized modulo scalars by P^1. On a line missing p the restricted presentation is (x,y,0), giving O + O(-1) and a unique map up to scalar to O_L(-1). Disjoint supports let the two line maps be rescaled independently, giving exactly one kernel for each unordered pair. The hull is determined by the common zero p (different bases of the three linear forms give isomorphic hulls), and the kernel recovers the hull and quotient by double duality and the quotient map up to equivalence; hull automorphisms are scalar by stability. For algebraicity of the conic count one can work over the open 11-dimensional space of parametrized degree-two embeddings of P^1: the degree -1 target then exists in family, and constant rank Hom with vanishing H^1 gives a relative P^1. Adding p off the plane and forgetting the parametrization (fibers PGL2 of dimension 3) gives dimension 12 and an irreducible constructible image. Ordered skew lines and p form an irreducible open parameter base of dimension 11; unordered pairs only remove a finite ordering. In both cases E agrees with the reflexive hull off codimension two, is slope-stable by inclusion with equal slope, and the pure quotient has ch(Q)=2H^2-4H^3 by RR. Subtracting from ch(F) yields c(E)=(-1,3,7). The computation neither needs nor proves that all quotients in the boundary have one of the two displayed types.

value.rationale: Gives exact structural dimensions of the families arising over the two generic degree-two target types in a named, unresolved moduli boundary, with a geometric explanation of the difference (a genuine pencil of distinct conic kernels versus a single skew-line kernel). This distinguishes contributions to the boundary that a target dimension count alone would conflate, and supplies reference strata for studying closures and incidence degenerations. It does not claim to settle the full boundary.
